title: Jio Platforms Gets SEBI Green Light for $3.8 Billion IPO, India's Biggest
excerpt: India's markets regulator cleared the Reliance subsidiary's offering on Friday, setting the stage for a listing that would surpass Hyundai Motor India's 2024 record.
body:
• SEBI issued final observations on Jio Platforms' draft prospectus on August 28, clearing the company to proceed with its $3.8 billion IPO.
  • The offering — a pure fresh issue of 270 million shares — would surpass Hyundai Motor India's 2024 listing as the largest IPO in Indian history.
  • Proceeds will primarily repay Rs 27,500 crore ($3.3 billion) in Reliance Jio Infocomm debt; none of Jio's major backers, including Meta and Google, plan to sell shares.

India's Securities and Exchange Board of India cleared Jio Platforms to proceed with a $3.8 billion initial public offering on Friday, removing the final regulatory hurdle for what would be the country's largest-ever stock market listing.

SEBI issued its final observations on the draft prospectus Jio filed in June, according to an update on the regulator's website. The approval allows the digital services arm of Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries to move ahead with preparations for the public offering.

IPO Structure and Use of Proceeds

Jio Platforms plans to issue up to 270 million fresh equity shares, representing about 2.9 percent of its post-issue equity base. At the expected issue size of roughly Rs 37,700 crore ($3.8 billion), the offering would value the company at approximately $137 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=rJJSHnTOP6Y

The bulk of the proceeds — about Rs 27,500 crore ($3.3 billion) — will go toward repaying outstanding borrowings of Reliance Jio Infocomm, Jio Platforms' material subsidiary. The remainder is earmarked for general corporate purposes.

The offering is structured as a pure fresh issue with no offer-for-sale component, meaning none of Jio's existing shareholders plan to sell shares in the IPO. Analysts have noted this signals confidence: the capital goes directly into the business rather than serving as a liquidity event for early investors.

India's Second-Largest Mobile Operator Goes Public

Jio Platforms houses Reliance's digital businesses, anchored by its telecommunications operations. Reliance Jio Infocomm had more than 533 million subscribers as of June-end, making it the world's second-largest mobile operator by subscriber count after China Mobile. The company commands roughly 60 percent of India's data traffic.

Beyond telecom, Jio has expanded into AI, cloud computing, and enterprise network services — a diversification push that underpins its valuation premium over pure-play carriers.

The company's operating performance has been strong. For the March quarter of fiscal year 2026, Jio reported a 13 percent year-on-year rise in operating revenue to Rs 44,928 crore, with net profit climbing 13 percent to Rs 7,935 crore. EBITDA grew 18 percent as operating margins expanded by 230 basis points.

Who Owns What

Reliance Industries holds about 66.4 percent of Jio Platforms. Meta owns roughly 9.9 percent and Google about 7.7 percent, according to the draft prospectus. In 2020, Jio raised funds from a string of marquee global investors — including Meta, Google, Vista Equity Partners, and KKR — diluting about 33 percent of its equity. Jefferies has previously valued the business at $180 billion.

None of these investors plan to sell in the IPO. The all-fresh-issue structure stands in contrast to several recent Indian offerings that were primarily driven by secondary sales from private equity and venture capital backers.

Record-Setting in a Hot Market

If Jio raises the targeted amount, it would surpass Hyundai Motor India's $2.95 billion listing in 2024 as the largest IPO in Indian history. A proposed listing by the National Stock Exchange, estimated at about Rs 30,000 crore, would also be smaller.

The approval comes as India's primary market remains active. More than two dozen IPOs have been announced or launched since July 1, nearly matching the 28 recorded in the first half of 2026, driven by strong participation from retail investors and domestic institutions.

"I believe this is the right time for Jio to come into the primary market and get listed on stock exchanges."

— Kranthi Bathini, Director of Equity Strategy, WealthMills Securities

What Comes Next

With SEBI's green light secured, Jio Platforms can now file its final prospectus and set an IPO date. Market participants expect the listing within the next few months, though the exact timeline will depend on market conditions and Reliance's strategic planning.

For NRI investors, the listing presents both opportunity and complication. Indian securities regulations restrict overseas investors from participating directly in domestic IPOs through standard retail channels — a constraint that could leave many diaspora investors on the sidelines unless they hold demat accounts with Indian brokers.

The listing would also give global investors a cleaner way to value Jio independently of parent Reliance Industries, whose conglomerate structure spans energy, retail, and telecommunications.
